how_to: Fill each cup of a muffin tin with a ball or small toy and set it on the floor in front of your baby. Let them pull everything out, then show how to put one back. Most babies dump first and fill later, closer to 11 months.
materials: balls or toys that fit the cups
safety_notes: Use balls and toys labeled safe for under-1s and too large to choke on; put them away after play.

title: Ball through the tube
summary: Drop a ball into a clear tube and watch it fall out the bottom into a basket.
how_to: Tape a clear tube to the wall at a height your baby can reach while sitting or standing with support, with a basket underneath. Show how the ball goes in the top and drops out the bottom, then hand them the ball. For a variation, lean the tube on a pillow like a slide.
safety_notes: Use a ball too large to swallow and check the tape stays secure.

title: Heuristic treasure basket
summary: A basket of everyday natural, wood, metal, and fabric objects for open-ended exploration.
how_to: Fill a low basket with clean, safe everyday objects: a pinecone, a large shell, a wooden spoon, a metal lid, fabric scraps. Set it out and let your baby explore freely while you watch. Rotate items often to keep interest.
safety_notes: Check every object is too large to swallow, clean, and free of sharp edges or loose bits; pinecones should be large and intact. Supervise mouthing.

title: Photo books and the real thing
summary: Look at books with real photographs, then go find the real object in your home.
how_to: Choose a board book with photos. Name and talk about what your baby sees, even things not in the text. When you see something you own, like a shoe or a banana, pause and go get the real one to hold next to the picture.

title: Water bowl on the grass
summary: Takes last month's indoor water tray outside: a bowl of water and nesting cups on the grass for filling and pouring.
how_to: Once your baby sits steadily, take them outside on a warm day. Set a large bowl with a little water and a few nesting cups on the grass, deck, or patio. Let them scoop, pour, splash, and feel the grass.
safety_notes: Drowning risk: use very little water and stay within arm's reach the whole time. Use sun protection and check the area for small objects and plants your baby could mouth.

title: Cruising aisle between two pieces of furniture
summary: Set two sturdy surfaces side by side so your baby can cruise while holding on with both hands.
how_to: Place a couch and a low table parallel, with just enough room for your baby to stand between them. Sit at the far end and invite your baby to cruise toward an interesting toy you hold. Let your baby go barefoot for better feedback through the feet.
safety_notes: Use only furniture that cannot tip. Pad or cover sharp corners and clear the floor of small objects.

title: Squat-to-stand and tall kneel at a low table
summary: Help your baby feel the movement from squatting to standing and back, and play in a tall kneel.
how_to: Sit on the floor with your baby on your lap in front of a coffee table. Guide their hips up to standing, then help them lower back down. Another time, set a toy on the table so your baby reaches for it while kneeling with their bottom lifted off their heels.
safety_notes: Use a surface that won't slide or tip. Keep hands close to catch backward falls.

title: Egg in cup and palmar block
summary: Classic Montessori pieces that let your baby lift out and replace a wooden egg or cylinder.
how_to: Offer the egg in its cup first; it is forgiving and can be grasped with the whole hand. Once your baby removes and replaces it easily, offer a palmar block, where a cylinder must go back in upright. Show the movement slowly once, then let your baby try.
safety_notes: Check pieces are too large to fit in the mouth fully and have no cracks or loose paint.

title: Pom-pom whisk challenge
summary: Your baby pinches pom-poms out from between the wires of a whisk.
how_to: Push a few pom-poms between the wires of a balloon whisk. Hand it to your baby and show how to pull one out with thumb and finger. Let them hold the whisk in one hand and pull with the other, and offer a bowl to drop the pom-poms into.
safety_notes: Pom-poms are a choking hazard. Stay right beside your baby, stop if they mouth them, and put them away after play.

title: Wave hello and bye-bye
summary: Build waving into everyday comings and goings so your baby learns the gesture by copying.
how_to: Gently wave your baby's hand while saying "Hi!" or "Bye-bye!" Wave every time you leave a room or put them down for a nap. When your baby waves, wave back and name it.

title: Name it near your mouth
summary: Hold objects near your mouth as you name them so your baby connects the word, the sound, and the thing.
how_to: Pick up an everyday object, hold it close to your face, and say its name clearly. Point to yourself when you say "mama" or "dada." Keep it relaxed and talk about what you're doing through the day.
safety_notes: Use objects too large to choke on.

title: Drop and pause: answering your baby's signals
summary: Drop a ball into a tube, pause, and respond warmly to any look, gesture, or sound your baby makes.
how_to: Sit facing your baby with a clear tube and a few balls. Drop a ball in, then wait. If your baby makes eye contact, waves, or vocalizes, respond right away with words and a smile, then take another turn.
safety_notes: Use balls larger than a toilet-paper-roll opening so they can't be swallowed.

title: Scarf peekaboo
summary: A light play scarf turns peekaboo into a back-and-forth game your baby can lead.
how_to: Drape a thin scarf over your face and pull it off with "Peekaboo!" Then cover a toy and let your baby pull the scarf away. Hand the scarf to your baby and wait to see if they cover their own face.
safety_notes: Supervise scarf play and don't leave scarves near a sleeping baby.

title: Family photo flap frames
summary: Homemade flaps hide photos of family members for your baby to find.
how_to: Glue wipe-container lids (or cardboard flaps) on three sides to a large piece of cardboard and slide a family photo into each. Open one flap and say, "Who's there? It's Daddy!" Let your baby open the rest, and swap photos regularly.
safety_notes: Supervise and put the board away after play; check lids stay firmly glued.

title: In-and-out containers
summary: Simple containers meet your baby's urge to put things in and take them out.
how_to: Offer a small bucket with one chunky puzzle piece, a jar with one small figure, or an imbucare box. Model putting the object in once, then step back. Let your baby find their own ways to use them.
safety_notes: Choose objects too large to swallow. Use a plastic or sturdy jar and supervise.

title: House tour for the senses
summary: Carry your baby around the home and explore real things by touch, sight, and sound.
how_to: Run their fingers over a houseplant's leaves, open and close a creaking door, and watch a ceiling fan spin. Let them feel water from the tap and touch different fruits and vegetables. Name everything as you go.
safety_notes: Check tap water temperature first. Avoid plants that are toxic if mouthed.

title: Couscous scoop and pour bin
summary: A shallow bin of dry couscous to scoop, pour, and feel.
how_to: Fill a shallow bin with uncooked couscous or another dry grain. Show how to scoop with a measuring cup and pour it out, then let your baby try. Describe how it feels and sounds.
safety_notes: Supervise at all times and don't let your baby eat the uncooked grain. Put materials away after play.

title: Standing diaper changes
summary: Once your baby pulls to stand, change wet diapers while they stand holding a support.
how_to: Set up a spot with a low bar, stool, or furniture to hold, with diapers and wipes within reach. Let your baby stand and hold on while you change the diaper. Invite them to help open tabs and lift a leg.
materials: sturdy support to hold (bar, stool, or furniture)
safety_notes: Use a non-slip floor surface and keep wipes and creams out of the mouth.

title: Cruising challenges: corners, gaps, and turns
summary: Make cruising harder by adding corners, small gaps, and turns once your baby cruises in a straight line.
how_to: Arrange furniture so your baby has to round a corner or reach across a small gap between a couch and a low table. Offer a toy slightly out of reach along the route. Stand behind your baby and offer a toy so they turn their body to take it.
safety_notes: Keep gaps small enough to reach safely. Pad sharp corners and use furniture that cannot tip.

title: Low platform and ramp
summary: A low platform or firm cushion gives your baby a place to climb up a step, climb down, and cruise.
how_to: Set up a low platform with a ramp, or a firm alternative like a foam play couch, low ottoman, or crib mattress. Let your baby climb, kneel, bear-crawl up, slide down backward, and cruise around the edge. Stay close but let them work out the moves.
materials: Pikler platform and ramp, or foam play couch / low ottoman / crib mattress
safety_notes: Climbing: keep it low, place soft flooring around it, and stay within reach.

title: Sticky note wall
summary: Sticky notes at different heights invite your baby to pull up to stand and reach.
how_to: Stick notes on a wall, kitchen island, or other safe vertical surface. Place some low enough to reach while sitting and some higher so your baby pulls up to grab them. Lovevery suggests this around 11–12 months.
safety_notes: Supervise so paper isn't chewed and swallowed. Use a surface your baby can't pull over.

title: Key ring slide
summary: Your baby pinches a key and slides it up a ring, then lets it drop.
how_to: Hold a baby-safe key ring steady and show how to pinch one key and slide it to the top. Let it drop back down with a fun sound effect. Hold a key out for your baby to try.
materials: baby-safe stainless steel key ring (not real keys)
safety_notes: Don't use real keys; they can be dirty, sharp, or contain lead.

title: First sips from an open cup
summary: Offer a tiny open cup with a little water while you hold it, until your baby reaches to hold it too.
how_to: Pour a small amount of water into a 1–2 oz cup. With your baby on your lap facing out, bring the cup to their mouth and tip it gently. Keep offering small amounts at meals; spills are part of learning.
materials: 1–2 oz open cup (shot-glass size or small silicone cup)
safety_notes: Use very small amounts to avoid sputtering. Only offer small amounts of water after 6 months. Use tempered glass or silicone if your baby bites or throws.

title: Wave to a doll in the mirror
summary: Build on last month's waving: now your baby practices hello and bye-bye with a doll or stuffed animal at the mirror.
how_to: Sit with your baby in front of a mirror holding a favorite doll or stuffed animal. Hide the toy, bring it back, and wave "Hello!"; hide it again with "Bye-bye!" Wave back whenever your baby waves.
safety_notes: Use an acrylic or safety-backed mirror.

title: Back-and-forth babble chat
summary: Repeat your baby's sounds and pause so they learn conversation is a turn-taking game.
how_to: Sit face to face. When your baby babbles, repeat the sound back, then pause and wait for their reply. Keep going for a few rounds, smiling and making eye contact.

title: "In! Out!" narration
summary: Say the same short words every time your baby fills or dumps a container.
how_to: Fill a basket with safe objects like balls, blocks, and balled-up socks. Each time your baby drops something in, say "In! In!" and each time they dump it out, say "Out! Boom!" Keep the words consistent so they link the word and the action.
safety_notes: Use objects too big to swallow; avoid long ribbons that could wrap around the neck.

title: Glove finger-puppet feelings show
summary: Faces drawn on a kitchen glove put on a short puppet show about feelings.
how_to: Draw happy, sad, mad, scared, and surprised faces on the fingertips of a kitchen glove. Hold your hand about a foot from your baby and narrate a short show, matching your voice to each face. Pause and let your baby reach or babble back.
materials: kitchen glove or paper finger tubes
safety_notes: Don't leave the glove with your baby; latex and paper can be chewed off.

title: Lap-bounce rhymes
summary: Bouncing rhymes like "Trot, Trot to Boston" build anticipation and shared fun.
how_to: Sit your baby on your knees facing you. Bounce gently through "Trot, trot to Boston, trot, trot to Lynn," then hold them securely and dip on "you don't fall in!" Try "This Is the Way the Baby Rides" with slow and fast bounces.
safety_notes: Hold your baby firmly under the arms during dips; keep bounces gentle.

title: Short, warm goodbye
summary: A calm, predictable goodbye helps a baby who is wary of new people.
how_to: When leaving your baby with someone new, stay for the first 10–15 minutes. Then say goodbye, wave, and tell your baby you'll be back. Don't sneak away or drag out the goodbye.

title: Box with sliding lid
summary: A sliding lid hides and reveals a small object, a step up from the object permanence box.
how_to: Place a small toy or wooden shape in one side of the box. Slide the lid over to hide it and back to reveal it. Let your baby slide it themselves; at first they may only play with the object.
safety_notes: Use objects too large to swallow; watch fingers in the sliding track.

title: Muffin tin fill and empty
summary: Twelve cups in one: your baby moves balls or toys in and out of a muffin tin.
how_to: Fill a muffin tin with balls or small toys and set it on the floor. Show how to take them out and put them back one at a time. Many babies start putting things back in around 11 months.
safety_notes: Use toys recommended for babies under 1 that are too big to swallow; supervise and put away after.

title: Single-shape puzzle
summary: A one-piece knobbed circle puzzle teaches in and out without having to sort shapes.
how_to: Start with a single circle piece. Show your baby how to lift it out by the knob and set it back. Add a square, then a triangle, one at a time, once each is mastered.
safety_notes: Check the knob is firmly attached and can't come off.

title: Baby-height dressing spot
summary: Move dressing from the changing table to a low corner where your baby can stand, hold on, and help.
how_to: Set up a corner with a pull-up bar or sturdy support, a small chair, and a laundry basket. Dress your baby while they stand or sit there, inviting them to push an arm through a sleeve. Let them drop dirty clothes in the basket.
safety_notes: Make sure the support is anchored and the chair can't tip.

title: Paint-in-a-bag color mixing
summary: Dollops of paint sealed in a bag with a canvas let your baby mix colors with no mess.
how_to: Put dollops of red, yellow, and blue tempera paint on a small canvas and slide it into a freezer bag. Seal it and tape it to the floor or high-chair tray. Let your baby squish the colors around, then take out the canvas to dry.
safety_notes: Tape the bag seal closed and check for leaks; supervise so it isn't bitten open.

title: Nature walk and treasure box
summary: A slow neighborhood walk to look, touch, smell, and collect a few natural treasures.
how_to: Stop often so your baby can see grass, bark, moss, leaves, and stones up close. Help them run a hand along tree bark and smell flowers or herbs. Collect one of each item in a basket to explore again at home.
safety_notes: Keep small stones, berries, and mushrooms out of the mouth. Avoid plants that may be toxic.

title: Weighted push wagon
summary: A sturdy wagon, slowed down with heavy books, for a baby who already pulls up and stands steadily.
how_to: Wait until your baby pulls up on the wagon by themselves; don't stand them behind it. Put a few heavy books inside so it rolls slowly. Clear a path and let them push at their own pace.
safety_notes: Choose a wagon with a wide base that won't tip backward. Keep away from stairs and clear the path of cords.

title: Two-handled basket walk
summary: You and your baby hold a basket together and step along a line of toys, squatting to pick each one up.
how_to: Line up small toys on the floor. Hold one handle of a two-handled basket and let your baby hold the other. Step toward the first toy, show how to pick it up and drop it in, then move to the next one together.
safety_notes: Use toys too large to swallow and a clear floor. Expect falls onto the bottom and stay close.

title: Barefoot steps with a pinky hold
summary: Progression from cruising: support early steps with a light hold at shoulder height, barefoot on a firm floor.
how_to: Let your baby go barefoot on a wood or firm floor. Offer your pinky finger at or below their shoulder instead of holding both hands overhead. When they fall, stay calm and describe it: "You sat down. You can get back up."
safety_notes: Pad sharp corners and move cords and breakables out of reach. Check outdoor surfaces for sharp objects before going barefoot.

title: Cubes on a vertical dowel
summary: Your baby pulls wooden cubes off a dowel and, around 12 months, starts threading them back on.
how_to: Present the dowel with cubes stacked on it. Let your baby pull them off and explore. Show slowly how to slide one cube back on, then let them try.
safety_notes: Cubes should be too big to swallow; check the dowel is fixed firmly to its base.

title: Chips in a slotted box
summary: For babies who have mastered posting a ball: push flat chips through a narrow slot.
how_to: Cut a slot in the lid of a shoe box just wider than a poker chip. Show how to turn a chip to fit and push it through. Open the lid to get them back out.
materials: shoe box with slot cut in lid
poker chips or large wooden coins
safety_notes: Chips are a choking hazard for babies who still mouth. Supervise closely, count them in and out, and store out of reach.

title: Stacking natural loose parts
summary: Large natural objects like wooden rings, big corks, and smooth pebbles to stack and arrange.
how_to: Put a few large wooden rings, chunky corks, and smooth palm-sized stones in a shallow tray. Let your baby handle, stack, and knock them over. Name what they do: "On top! Fall down!"
safety_notes: Small parts: every item must be too big to fit in a toilet-paper-roll tube. Supervise closely while your baby still mouths objects.

title: Kitchen vocabulary basket
summary: A basket of 5–8 real kitchen objects that you name as your baby explores them.
how_to: Fill a basket with 5–8 kitchen items such as a whisk, wooden spoon, and small pot. Name each one as your baby picks it up. Ask, "Can you find the whisk?" If they do, say "You found the whisk"; if not, just name what they picked.
materials: 5–8 kitchen objects (whisk, wooden spoon, small pot, cup, sieve)
safety_notes: Use unbreakable items with no sharp edges or small detachable parts.

title: Bath words: first sounds, body parts, in and out
summary: Repeat simple bath words and pair "in" and "out" with a clear gesture.
how_to: Stress early-sound words like bubble, ball, boat, pour, and pop. Name body parts as you wash. Say "Put the ball IN!" and "Take the ball OUT!" while showing the action, and ask "Where did the ball go?" with palms up.
safety_notes: Water: stay within arm's reach the whole time; babies can drown in very little water.

title: Caring for a baby doll
summary: A simple soft doll invites your baby to copy care they've received: blankets, feeding, strolling.
how_to: Offer a soft doll with a small blanket and toy bottle. Show one simple care action, like covering the doll for a nap or giving it the bottle. Let your baby copy and lead.
safety_notes: Choose a doll without small buttons or hair that can come off.

title: "If You're Happy and You Know It" clapping
summary: An action song that pairs feelings with clapping and stomping.
how_to: Sing "If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands," clapping big. Add "stomp your feet" and "shout hooray." Pause before each action so your baby can join.

title: Reunion minutes
summary: After time apart, give your baby 5–10 minutes of full attention before getting on with chores.
how_to: When you get home, sit with your baby before starting anything else. Read a book, go outside, or tell them about your day face to face. Add touch: a cuddle, a rock, or a gentle massage.

title: DIY ball chute box
summary: Balls dropped into holes in a propped-up box vanish and roll out the bottom.
how_to: Cut a few ball-sized holes in the top of a long cardboard box. Prop one end on the couch with the low end open, over a basket if you like. Give your baby a ball to drop in, then go find where it comes out.
safety_notes: Adults only for cutting. Use balls too big to swallow; tape any rough cardboard edges.

title: Ball pounding with a hammer
summary: Progression from pushing balls through with a palm: now try the wooden hammer.
how_to: Set the ball-pounding toy on a tray. Let your baby push the balls through with their hand, then offer the hammer once they have more arm control. Show one slow tap, then hand it over.
safety_notes: Supervise hammer use so it isn't swung at people; balls should be too big to swallow.

title: Drop it in the bowl
summary: An early gravity game: drop soft or wooden objects into a big bowl or laundry basket.
how_to: Place a large bowl, bucket, or laundry basket close by. Show how to drop a scarf, a crumpled paper, or a block into it and watch what falls fast or slow. Start with dropping from just above the container before trying small tosses.
materials: large bowl, bucket, or laundry basket
safety_notes: Use objects too large to swallow; supervise paper so it isn't eaten.

title: Little helper jobs
summary: Simple real jobs: laundry into the hamper, wiping the table with a rag, sweeping with a hand broom.
how_to: Invite your baby to drop clothes in the hamper, wipe the table with a small cloth after meals, or explore a hand broom. Show the motion slowly and let them try. It won't be done well, and that's fine.
safety_notes: Choose a broom with natural bristles and no small parts; keep cleaning chemicals out of reach.

title: Sealed sound jars
summary: Sealed plastic bottles filled with rice, sand, or beads make different sounds to shake and compare.
how_to: Fill a few small plastic bottles partway with different materials such as rice, sand, or beads. Glue and tape the lids shut. Shake one, then hand it over, and compare loud and soft sounds together.
safety_notes: Contents are a choking hazard: glue and tape lids shut, check before each use, and discard cracked bottles.

title: Push a big box across the floor
summary: Your toddler pushes a tall cardboard box or toy cart, which builds the balance they need before pulling toys.
how_to: Give your toddler a tall, empty cardboard box, toy stroller, or small shopping cart on a smooth floor. Let them lean on it and push it from room to room. Clear a path and let them work out what happens when it bumps into furniture.
materials: tall cardboard box or toy stroller
safety_notes: Clear sharp corners and rugs that slip from the path. Stay close while your toddler is still unsteady.

title: Creep up and down a low incline
summary: Your toddler crawls and walks up a gentle ramp or low step, building the strength that supports walking.
how_to: Set up a low, stable incline such as a wedge cushion, a ramp, or the bottom stair. Let your toddler creep up with knees, then try pushing up with feet. Spot them, but let them move their own body instead of lifting them.
materials: wedge cushion, foam ramp, or bottom stair
safety_notes: Spot from close by on climbing surfaces, use a soft landing area, and keep climbing structures away from hard edges.

title: Pop-up peg toy
summary: Your toddler pulls pegs out and works to fit them back in the holes.
how_to: Put a pop-up peg toy (or a block with chunky pegs) on a low shelf. Let your toddler remove all the pegs and try putting them back. Don't correct them; they will start turning pegs the right way up on their own.
materials: pop-up peg toy or peg-and-hole board
safety_notes: Choose pegs too large to fit in a toddler's mouth.

title: Toy rescue from painter's tape
summary: Your toddler picks at strips of tape to free small animals stuck to a tray.
how_to: Tape a few small animal figures or blocks to a baking sheet with painter's tape. Hand it to your toddler and say, 'Can you rescue the animals?' Let them use their fingertips to lift the tape edges and pull the toys free.
safety_notes: Use figures too big to swallow and collect the used tape so it isn't chewed.

title: Follow their point and name it
summary: When your toddler points, you look and name what they see, which links pointing to words.
how_to: Watch where your toddler points and name it in a short sentence: 'You see a squirrel! It's running up the tree.' Point too, while naming things around the house or outside. Keep it back-and-forth and follow their interest.

title: Kitchen vocabulary basket
summary: Progression from the month-12 kitchen basket: swap in new objects (e.g. a strainer) and ask your toddler to find each one by name.
how_to: Put 5-8 kitchen items in a basket: a whisk, wooden spoon, small pot, strainer. Name each one as your toddler explores it. Later ask, 'Can you find the whisk?' If they pick something else, simply name what they found.
safety_notes: Skip glass, sharp, or very small utensils. Expect mouthing and keep items clean.

title: Clapping games with a reliable response
summary: You answer your toddler's clap or game invitation the same way every time, so they learn they can start a shared game.
how_to: When your toddler claps or covers their face, respond the same way each time: play pat-a-cake, or say 'Where did you go?' Repeat as often as they want. The predictable reply teaches them they can cause a reaction from you.

title: Name the feeling
summary: You describe what your toddler did and connect it to a feeling, so they start linking emotions to actions.
how_to: When a strong moment happens, narrate it: 'Your cracker broke and you started crying. You seem sad.' Or: 'You're jumping because Grandma is here. You're excited!' Keep it short and calm, and offer a hug if they want one.

title: Ring stacker back-and-forth
summary: You and your toddler take turns putting rings on a peg as they shift from taking rings off to stacking them.
how_to: Have your toddler hand you the rings and stack them one at a time. Then pass the rings back and see if they try. Tilt the peg toward them to make it easier. Order and size don't matter yet.
safety_notes: Choose rings too large to fit in the mouth.

title: Hide toys in the laundry basket
summary: Your toddler digs under clothes or tissue paper to find toys you hid, practising object permanence.
how_to: Put a few favourite toys in a laundry basket and cover them with clothes or tissue paper while your toddler watches. Ask, 'Where's the ball?' Let them dig. Swap roles and let them hide toys for you to find.
safety_notes: Use toys without small parts.

title: Sponge squeezing
summary: Your toddler squeezes water out of sponges, feeling how water moves.
how_to: Put a little water in a shallow tub with one or two sponges, ideally natural sponges of different textures. Show how you squeeze the water out, then let your toddler try. Do it outside or on a towel.
safety_notes: Never leave a toddler alone near water, even a shallow tub. Stay within arm's reach and empty containers after play.

title: Basket of instruments to bang and shake
summary: A small basket of real instruments invites your toddler to make sounds and play with you.
how_to: Put two or three good-sounding instruments in a basket, such as a tambourine, a shaker, and a small drum. Play alongside them and copy their rhythms. Rotate instruments so the basket stays interesting.
safety_notes: Check shakers are sealed so beads can't escape. Avoid very loud instruments close to ears.

title: Nature basket
summary: Progression from month 12's nature basket: your toddler now helps collect the natural objects and explores textures, shapes, and weights.
how_to: Collect a few natural objects with your toddler: large pinecones, smooth stones, bark, big shells. Put them in a shallow basket and let your toddler handle them freely. Name each texture: rough, smooth, heavy, light.
safety_notes: Choose items bigger than your toddler's mouth, check for sharp edges, and supervise for mouthing.

title: Carry, push, and haul (maximum effort)
summary: New walkers love to carry, push, and pull heavy-ish things, which challenges balance and strength.
how_to: Leave out a few safe things to haul: a small stool to push, a bucket to fill and carry, a child-size broom or rake. Let your toddler move them from room to room. Step back and let them work hard, even if it looks slow.
safety_notes: Keep loads light enough that a fall won't hurt, and clear stairs and sharp corners from their route.

title: Walk between two stable things
summary: Your toddler takes a few steps across a short gap between furniture, building confidence to walk alone.
how_to: Place two sturdy pieces of furniture (couch and ottoman, or two low stools) a short step apart. Put an interesting object on one side. Let your toddler work out how to cross. Don't move the furniture once they start.
safety_notes: Use furniture that can't tip or slide, and pad hard floors around the gap.

title: Roll a ball back and forth
summary: You roll a large soft ball to your toddler and see if they can roll or push it back.
how_to: Sit on the floor facing each other with legs apart. Roll a large soft ball to your toddler and say 'Roll it to me!' while holding out your hands. Cheer for any push back toward you.
safety_notes: Use a soft ball and play away from breakables.

title: Peel banana slices
summary: Your toddler peels pre-sliced banana rounds and drops the skins in a bowl, a first food-prep job.
how_to: Slice a banana into rounds with the peel on and cut a small slit in each peel. Give your toddler a plate of rounds and a bowl for skins. Show once how to pull the peel off, then let them peel and eat.
safety_notes: Offer soft, toddler-safe pieces and keep your child seated while eating to lower choking risk.

title: Felt pocket hide
summary: Your toddler pushes small toys into felt pockets and pulls them out again.
how_to: Glue the edges of two felt squares together on three sides to make a pocket, or use a small zip pouch. Show your toddler how a ring or a small block fits inside. Let them stuff and empty the pockets as often as they like.
safety_notes: Small parts are a choking hazard. Stay within reach and put pieces away after play.

title: Cereal scoop in a muffin tin
summary: Your toddler scoops and pours O-shaped cereal between muffin cups.
how_to: Fill a few cups of a muffin tin with O-shaped cereal. Add small measuring cups or spoons. Invite your toddler to scoop, pour, and pinch the cereal into other cups or piles. Eating some is fine.
safety_notes: Offer soft, toddler-safe pieces and keep your child seated while eating to lower choking risk.

title: Photo books, expanded
summary: Short daily reading with real-photo books, where you turn your toddler's single words into short phrases.
how_to: Pick a board book with clear photos of familiar things. Read for a few minutes at a time, several times a day. If your toddler says 'baw' for ball, reply, 'Yes, ball! A big yellow ball.' Let them turn pages and skip around.

title: Simple requests with a gesture
summary: You ask simple questions and requests and watch how your toddler answers with their body.
how_to: Ask things like 'Where's the dog?' or 'Hand me the spoon, please,' and hold out your hand or glance at the object as you speak. Watch whether they turn, look, or hand it over. Thank them and name the object.

title: Two simple signs: 'all done' and 'milk'
summary: A couple of simple gestures give your toddler a way to ask for what they need before they have the words.
how_to: Pick one or two gestures, like waving flat hands for 'all done' or squeezing a fist for 'milk.' Use the gesture and the word together every time at meals. When your toddler tries the gesture, respond right away.

title: Blanket on the doll
summary: Early imitative play: your toddler copies what you do, like tucking a blanket over a doll.
how_to: Offer a soft doll or stuffed animal and a small blanket. Show how you tuck it in and pat it, then hand it over. Accept whatever version your toddler does; this is copying, not a full story yet.

title: Mirror kisses and peekaboo
summary: In front of a mirror, your toddler sees you both, kisses their reflection, and plays peekaboo.
how_to: Sit with your toddler in front of a low, secure mirror. Say, 'I see Maya in the mirror!' Play peekaboo by ducking out of view and popping back. See if they'll blow a kiss or touch the reflection.
safety_notes: Use a shatterproof mirror fixed securely to the wall or furniture.

title: Small cup into big cup
summary: Your toddler learns to nest a smaller cup inside a bigger one.
how_to: Offer two or three nesting cups. Say, 'Watch how I put the small cup into the big cup,' and move slowly. If they try big-into-small, spread the cups out and show again. Add a third cup when two is easy.

title: Sliding-lid box
summary: A box with a sliding lid hides and reveals an object, a step up from simple drop-in boxes.
how_to: Put a small toy or teether inside a wooden box with a sliding lid (or a pencil box). Show your toddler how sliding the lid hides it and sliding it back reveals it. Leave it out so they can repeat on their own.
materials: sliding-lid wooden box or pencil box
safety_notes: Check the lid can't pinch fingers hard, and use objects too big to swallow.

title: What falls faster?
summary: Your toddler drops different objects and sees that some fall fast and some float down.
how_to: Hold your toddler while standing, and let them drop things one at a time: a scarf, a flat sheet of paper, a crumpled paper ball, a crayon. Say what you see: 'The scarf floats slowly. The crayon drops fast!' Expect many repeats.
safety_notes: Use light, unbreakable objects and drop them away from people.

title: Kitchen basics: bowl, hands, bin
summary: Your toddler starts kitchen work with three simple routines: getting their own bowl, washing hands, and throwing things away.
how_to: Store your toddler's bowl and spoon low where they can reach. Before snacks, wash hands in the same spot each time, then let them fetch their bowl. Afterward, show them where the bin is and let them toss in a napkin.
safety_notes: Use a sturdy step stool at the sink and keep knives and hot items out of reach.

title: Ice cube bowl
summary: Your toddler explores ice melting in a bowl of water and hears new words like cold and slippery.
how_to: Fill a large bowl with a little water and drop in a few ice cubes. Let your toddler touch, push, and chase the cubes. Use words like cold, melt, and slippery as they play.
safety_notes: Never leave a toddler alone near water, even a shallow tub. Stay within arm's reach and empty containers after play. Use large cubes and take them back if your toddler tries to put a whole cube in their mouth.

title: Flashlight shadows
summary: In a dim room you shine a flashlight behind objects so your toddler can watch shadows grow and shrink.
how_to: Darken a room and shine a flashlight at a wall. Hold a toy or your hand in the beam and move it closer and farther so the shadow changes size. Let your toddler hold the flashlight or wave their hands in the light.
safety_notes: Use a flashlight with a screwed-in battery cover, and don't shine it directly into eyes.

title: Cushion obstacle course
summary: A course of cushions, blankets, and tunnels gives a climbing toddler a safe place to move hard.
how_to: Pull couch cushions and pillows onto the floor to make mounds, a slide, and a low tower. Drape a blanket over chairs for a tunnel. Let your toddler crawl, climb, and walk over it, and help you put it all back at the end.
safety_notes: Spot from close by on climbing surfaces, use a soft landing area, and keep climbing structures away from hard edges.

title: Balance walk on a curb
summary: Holding your hand, your toddler steps along a low curb or log, practising balance.
how_to: On a walk, find a low curb, a fallen log, or a garden edge. Hold your toddler's hand and let them step along it, one foot at a time. Go slowly and let them step down when they want.
safety_notes: Choose curbs away from traffic and hold your toddler's hand the whole time.

title: Sit and toss into a basket
summary: Building on ball rolling, your toddler now sits and tosses a soft ball toward a basket.
how_to: Put a laundry basket close in front of your sitting toddler. Show how you toss a soft ball in, then guide their hand once and let them release on their own. Cheer every try and move the basket back only when it gets easy.
safety_notes: Use soft balls only, and throw toward the basket rather than at your toddler.

title: Shape sorter with one shape
summary: A shape sorter cut down to just the cylinder pieces gives your toddler a challenge they can finish.
how_to: Remove all pieces except the cylinders from a shape sorter. Show how one drops through the round hole, then let your toddler try. Add the square or triangle pieces only when the cylinders are easy.
safety_notes: Use pieces too big to fit in the mouth.

title: Unwrap a surprise
summary: Your toddler uses both hands to open small toys you have loosely wrapped in paper.
how_to: Loosely wrap a few familiar toys or books in scrap paper or newspaper, with no tape. Hand one over and let your toddler tear and pull the paper off. Rewrap and repeat.
safety_notes: Take paper away if your toddler starts eating it, and use toys without small parts.

title: Seated snack with real dishes
summary: Your toddler feeds themselves finger foods at a small table using a real plate and cup.
how_to: Seat your toddler at a low table or high chair with a real plate and a small glass. Offer a few soft finger foods at a time. Expect squishing and dropping; calmly show what to do instead and end the meal when they get up.
safety_notes: Offer soft, toddler-safe pieces and keep your child seated while eating to lower choking risk. Supervise closely with breakable dishes.

title: Bathtime words
summary: The bath is a good place to repeat early words like bubble, pour, and pop, plus 'in' and 'out'.
how_to: During the bath, stress words with early sounds: 'b-b-bubble,' 'pour,' 'more,' 'pop.' Put a ball or cup in and out of a container and say 'in!' and 'out!' each time. Pause and wait for your toddler to try a sound.
safety_notes: Never leave a toddler alone near water, even a shallow tub. Stay within arm's reach and empty containers after play.

title: Answer the babble
summary: When your toddler babbles at you and pauses, you answer as if you understood, keeping the conversation going.
how_to: If your toddler babbles alone after a nap, let it run without interrupting. When they babble to you and pause, reply with animation: 'Oh really? Then what happened?' Leave space for their turn.

title: Name body parts while washing
summary: You name the body parts your toddler can see as you wash, dress, and brush.
how_to: Start with parts they can see: hands, feet, belly, arms, legs. Name each as you wash it, put on socks, or clip nails: 'Now your feet.' Sometimes ask, 'Where are your hands?' and watch whether they look.

title: Pretend along: feed baby, then change
summary: Moving on from simple copying, you join a two-step pretend game with a doll and let your toddler choose what comes next.
how_to: When your toddler pretends to sip from a cup or feed a doll, join in. Keep it to two or three steps, like feeding the baby and then changing its diaper. Ask, 'What next? Does baby need a nap?' and stop when they lose interest.

title: Make me laugh
summary: When your toddler repeats a sound or action to get a laugh, add a word to extend their joke.
how_to: Notice when your toddler does something to make you giggle and laugh again. Add a sound or word to the joke: if they pop out from under a scarf, say a silly 'Hi!' each time. Take a turn hiding so they can copy you.

title: Sportscast a toy grab
summary: At a playdate, if your toddler grabs a toy, you calmly describe what happened for both children instead of punishing.
how_to: If the other child doesn't mind, do nothing. If someone is upset, describe it: 'Maria, you really wanted the bunny. Olivia, you didn't like when she took it.' Offer the upset child comfort or another toy. Keep groups small.

title: Circle puzzle, biggest and smallest first
summary: A puzzle with only round pieces lets your toddler place pieces without needing to rotate them.
how_to: Offer a circle puzzle. If your toddler gets frustrated, give only the largest and smallest pieces first. Once those go in, add the middle sizes one at a time. Dumping it out is part of the play too.

title: Find the matching one
summary: Your toddler starts matching two identical objects, like two red rings or two spoons.
how_to: Pick two pairs of identical familiar things, such as two same-colour rings and two wooden coins. Say what's the same about each pair. Hand your toddler one ring and ask them to pick up the one that matches. Point out matches at meals too, like two spoons.
safety_notes: Small parts are a choking hazard. Stay within reach and put pieces away after play.

title: Self-care basket
summary: A basket with a hairbrush, washcloth, and tissues invites your toddler to use real things the right way.
how_to: Put a small hairbrush, a washcloth, and a few tissues in a low basket near a mirror. Show how you brush your hair or wipe your nose, then let your toddler try on themselves, you, or a doll.

title: Montessori coat flip
summary: A simple trick lets your toddler put on their own coat: tag to toes, hands in holes, flip.
how_to: Lay your toddler's coat flat on the floor, open, with the tag nearest their feet. Say 'Tag to the toes,' help them stand there, then 'Hands in the holes,' and 'Flip!' as they swing it over their head. Show it with your coat too.
safety_notes: Make sure the flip area is clear of furniture edges.

title: Paint with water outside
summary: With a tub of water and a big brush, your toddler 'paints' a fence or the pavement and watches it dry.
how_to: Fill a small tub with water and give your toddler a wide paintbrush. Let them paint the pavement, a fence, or a wall. Point out how the marks fade as they dry, then paint again.
safety_notes: Never leave a toddler alone near water, even a shallow tub. Stay within arm's reach and empty containers after play.

title: Sound jars
summary: Sealed bottles filled with rice, beads, or sand let your toddler compare sounds as they shake them.
how_to: Fill three small clear plastic bottles with different things: rice, dried beans, sand. Glue or tape the lids shut. Give them to your toddler to shake, roll, and compare. Shake along and say 'loud' or 'quiet.'
safety_notes: Glue lids shut and check regularly for cracks; loose beans and beads are choking hazards.

title: First pull toy
summary: Once steady on their feet, your toddler pulls a toy on a string behind them and works out what to do when it snags.
how_to: Give your toddler a pull toy with a short string once they walk steadily. Let them pull it around the room and outdoors. When it tips or catches on a chair, wait before helping so they can try to solve it.
materials: pull toy with a short string
safety_notes: Keep strings short (under about 30 cm) and only use pull toys with supervision; store them out of reach afterward.

title: Weighted walker wagon
summary: A step on from pushing a box at 13 months: your toddler pushes a sturdier wagon loaded with blocks, which needs steadier balance.
how_to: Load a walker wagon or doll stroller with a few blocks so it rolls slowly. Let your toddler push it around the house and unload it somewhere new. As they get steadier, they will start walking without it.
safety_notes: Choose a wagon with a wide base that won't tip forward, and keep it away from stairs.

title: Climb the stairs
summary: Climbing a flight of stairs with you right behind is good 'maximum effort' work for a toddler who wants to climb everything.
how_to: Pick a time when you aren't rushed. Let your toddler climb up the stairs on hands and feet while you stay one step below. Show them how to come down backwards on their tummy, feet first.
safety_notes: Stay one step below your toddler the whole time, and use safety gates when you are not supervising.

title: First crayon tray
summary: A small tray with two or three chunky crayons and paper gives your toddler their own art space.
how_to: Put two or three rock crayons or small crayon chunks in a little dish on a tray with a few sheets of paper. Show your toddler how to carry the tray to a table. Sit and scribble on your own sheet beside them.
safety_notes: Crayons will be mouthed at first; use non-toxic crayons and supervise.

title: Toddler-size fork at meals
summary: A small real fork, placed next to their spoon, gives your toddler another utensil to try at meals.
how_to: Set a small metal toddler fork beside their spoon at meals. Model stabbing a soft piece of food on your own fork. Let your toddler choose which utensil to use, or hands; don't push it.
safety_notes: Offer soft, toddler-safe pieces and keep your child seated while eating to lower choking risk. Choose a fork with blunt, rounded tines.

title: Drink from a small glass
summary: Your toddler drinks from a small open glass at meals and learns to set it down without spilling.
how_to: Pour a little water, about an inch, into a small glass at the table. Show how you hold it with two hands, sip, and put it down flat. Keep a cloth nearby and refill in small amounts.
safety_notes: Use a sturdy, thick glass and supervise; clear away any broken pieces immediately.

title: Copy Me Cups: one-step directions
summary: Stacking cups with a picture and instruction on each, like 'touch your nose,' give practice following one-step directions.
how_to: Pull a cup from the stack and act out what's pictured while reading it aloud. Let your toddler copy you, then try reading just the words without acting. No cups? Make up simple instructions like 'touch your toes' and play the same way.
materials: Copy Me Cups (Lovevery Adventurer Play Kit) or your own list of simple actions

title: Use the real names
summary: Toddlers want to know the name of everything; you give exact words like 'beagle,' 'zucchini,' or 'excavator.'
how_to: As you go about your day, name things precisely: the kind of dog, the vegetable you are cutting, the bird in the tree. When your toddler says 'ba-ba' for ball, show you heard by using the real word: 'Yes, you threw the ball.' Look at them and give them time to talk.

title: Sing the next step
summary: Singing instructions, like a clean-up song, helps your toddler follow through on tricky transitions.
how_to: Make up short songs for routines: 'Clean up, clean up, everybody, everywhere,' or a song for getting out of the bath or into the car seat. Sing the same song every time so your toddler learns what it means.

title: Handwashing with a pitcher and bowl
summary: Your toddler learns to pump soap, rub, and rinse while you handle the pitcher and bowl.
how_to: Set a bowl on a low table with a small pitcher of water, a soap pump, and a towel. Pour the water yourself for now. Show slowly how to pump soap, rub hands, and rinse, then let your toddler do it. Expect splashing; let them explore the water.
safety_notes: Never leave a toddler alone near water, even a shallow tub. Stay within arm's reach and empty containers after play. Use lukewarm water.

title: Invite help with undressing
summary: When your toddler starts pulling off shoes or coats, invite them to do part of each dressing step.
how_to: Dress your toddler in easy clothes with few buttons or snaps. At each change, ask them to help: 'Push your arm through,' 'Pull off your sock.' Leave enough time so you aren't rushing them.

title: Books about everyday life
summary: You share books with realistic pictures of daily life, like visiting grandparents or getting ready in the morning.
how_to: Pick books with realistic pictures of things your toddler knows: meals, bath time, shopping, family. Snuggle up and look at a few pages together. Let them choose the book and stop when they're done.
materials: picture books with realistic everyday scenes

title: Sweep with a hand broom
summary: Your toddler copies you sweeping with a small hand broom and dustpan.
how_to: Keep a small hand broom and dustpan where your toddler can reach them. Sweep alongside them after meals and show how crumbs go into the pan. Don't redo their work while they watch.

title: Opening and closing basket
summary: A basket of old purses and boxes with different fastenings, each hiding a small object to find.
how_to: Collect a few old purses, pouches, and boxes with different openings: zipper, snap, drawstring, lid. Hide a small object in each. Put them in a basket and let your toddler work out how to open and close them.
materials: old purses or pouches with zippers and snaps
safety_notes: Small parts are a choking hazard. Stay within reach and put pieces away after play. Remove long straps and drawstrings.

title: Loud drum, quiet drum
summary: When banging gets loud, you take a turn and show how tapping lightly is quiet and hitting hard is loud.
how_to: When your toddler bangs on a drum or pot, ask for a turn. Tap very quietly and say, 'Light tap, quiet.' Then hit harder: 'Big hit, LOUD!' Take turns, then sum it up: 'We banged loudly and quietly.'

title: Homemade finger paint
summary: A simple flour-salt-water paint gives your toddler a messy sensory art experience.
how_to: Mix 1 cup flour, 1/2 cup salt, 1 1/2 cups water, and a few drops of food colouring. Tape paper to the table, strip your toddler to a diaper or smock, and let them paint with hands. Don't clean up until they are done.
safety_notes: The salt makes it unpleasant to eat, but supervise so your toddler doesn't eat it.

title: Knead bread dough
summary: You measure ingredients and your toddler adds them, stirs, and kneads a small piece of dough.
how_to: Measure out the ingredients for a simple bread or pizza dough. Let your toddler tip each one into the bowl and stir with a wooden spoon. Give them a small lump on a floured surface and show how to fold and push it with the heel of your hand.
safety_notes: Stand beside your toddler at the counter, keep them away from the hot oven, and don't let them eat raw dough.

title: Clay with hands and simple tools
summary: A lump of soft clay on a board lets your toddler squeeze, poke, and press with fists, palms, and fingertips.
how_to: Put a fist-sized lump of soft natural clay on a wooden board. Let your toddler press, pinch, and break it apart with their hands. Add one unusual tool, such as a potato masher, and a few drops of water to keep it soft.
safety_notes: Clay isn't food; supervise for mouthing and wash hands afterward.

title: Treasure collecting walk with a basket
summary: Your toddler carries a basket or bucket on a walk and squats to collect 'treasures' along the way.
how_to: Give your toddler a basket with two rigid handles or a small bucket. Walk slowly outside or around the house and let them pick up leaves, pinecones, or toys and put them in. Walking while carrying and squatting to pick up builds balance.
materials: basket with handles or small bucket
safety_notes: Check what goes in the basket; remove sharp items, berries, mushrooms, and anything small enough to swallow.

title: Carry the bucket together, walking backward
summary: You and your toddler carry a large bucket between you while they walk backward.
how_to: Put a few soft toys in a large bucket. Ask your toddler to help carry it across the room. Let them hold one edge and walk backward while you hold the other side and push gently and slowly.
safety_notes: Clear the floor behind your toddler and go slowly so they don't trip.

title: Talk them through a climb
summary: After stair climbing at 16 months, you now coach your toddler with words instead of hands as they climb a playground ladder or into the car seat.
how_to: At first, say nothing and watch. If they get stuck, remind them what worked before ('Last time you put your knee here') or describe what they're doing ('You're holding the rail'). Offer a 'what if' idea and point, rather than lifting them.
materials: low playground ladder or climbing structure
safety_notes: Spot from close by on climbing surfaces, use a soft landing area, and keep climbing structures away from hard edges.

title: Scoop balls from warm water
summary: Your toddler uses a spoon or small strainer to scoop floating balls from one bowl of warm water to another.
how_to: Fill one bowl with warm water and a few practice golf balls or ping pong balls, and put an empty bowl beside it. Give your toddler a wooden spoon or small strainer. Let them scoop, drip, and transfer the balls on a towel.
materials: 4-5 ping pong or practice golf balls
safety_notes: Never leave a toddler alone near water, even a shallow tub. Stay within arm's reach and empty containers after play.

title: Watercolour with one colour
summary: Moving on from crayons, your toddler dips a brush in water, then a watercolour cake, then paper.
how_to: Set up a tray with one watercolour cake, a brush, a small jar with a little water, paper, and a cloth. Show the steps once: water, colour, paper. Using one colour keeps it simple and avoids muddy brown.
safety_notes: Use only a small amount of water and keep the jar on the tray to reduce spills.

title: Pour your own water
summary: After practising with a small glass at 16 months, your toddler now pours water from a small jug into it.
how_to: Put a small jug with a little water and a small glass on a low table, with a sponge nearby. Show slowly how to hold the jug with two hands and pour. When water spills, hand them the sponge to wipe it up.
safety_notes: Fill the jug only partly, and use a sturdy glass under supervision.

title: 'Bring me your shoes'
summary: You give one-step requests without pointing, like 'Bring me your shoes,' to see what your toddler understands.
how_to: During routines, ask for one thing using only words, without looking or pointing at it: 'Bring me your shoes,' 'Get your hat.' Wait. If they don't follow, add a gesture and try again another day.

title: Construction vehicle tray
summary: A small tray of realistic vehicles lets your toddler learn their names while pushing, parking, and lining them up.
how_to: Put 4-5 realistic vehicles on a tray: digger, dump truck, bulldozer, cement mixer. Name each as your toddler plays: 'The excavator is digging.' Repeat the names often, without quizzing.
safety_notes: Check for small detachable parts like wheels.

title: Say why with 'because'
summary: When your toddler watches you work, you tell them what you're doing and why.
how_to: When you notice your toddler watching you cook, dress them, or tidy up, describe it: 'I'm cutting this apple into pieces because that makes it easier to eat.' Keep sentences short. They understand more than they can say.

title: Slow noticing walk
summary: On an unhurried walk, your toddler wanders a little ahead and points out bugs, droplets, and flowers while you notice with them.
how_to: Go somewhere safe and green with no time pressure. Let your toddler lead and stop where they want. When they point, look with them and name it: 'A snail on the leaf!' Notice that they check back to see where you are.
safety_notes: Stay within a few steps, especially near roads or water, and check for stinging plants.

title: Bath-routine helper
summary: Your toddler helps with each step of the bath routine while you name the order: first, next, then.
how_to: Before the bath, ask your toddler to fetch their pajamas and a towel from the drawer. Let them help turn the tap (you check the temperature) and pump the soap. Narrate as you go: 'First the towel, next the water, then soap.'
safety_notes: Never leave a toddler alone near water, even a shallow tub. Stay within arm's reach and empty containers after play. Always check the water temperature yourself.

title: Window watching and pointing
summary: Sitting at a window, you and your toddler take turns pointing out things outside and naming them.
how_to: Sit at a window with a view of a street or yard. Point at something and name it: 'Look, a bus!' Then wait for your toddler to point at something. Name what they show you and add one detail.
safety_notes: Keep windows locked or fitted with guards, and don't let your toddler climb onto the sill or furniture beside it.

title: Stacking peg board
summary: Your toddler fits small pegs into a peg board and stacks them into towers, which can lead to colour matching.
how_to: Put the peg board and a few pegs on a tray. Show how a peg fits in a hole and how another stacks on top. Let your toddler build and knock down towers. Name colours as you play, but don't correct them.
materials: Wooden Stacking Peg Board (Lovevery Adventurer Play Kit) or similar peg board
safety_notes: Small parts are a choking hazard. Stay within reach and put pieces away after play.

title: Wipe up spills
summary: Your toddler copies you wiping up spills with a small cloth or towel.
how_to: Keep a few small cloths in a low basket near where your toddler eats. When something spills, hand them a cloth and wipe beside them. Let them wipe their tray or table after meals too.

title: Ramp race
summary: Your toddler sends cars, balls, and other objects down a homemade ramp and sees which slide or roll fastest.
how_to: Prop a piece of stiff cardboard against the couch. Give your toddler a wooden car, a ball, crumpled paper, and something that won't roll, like a banana. Say, 'Let's see which one is fastest!' and race them together.
safety_notes: Tape the ramp in place so it doesn't slide.

title: Rain walk
summary: With the right clothes, a rainy walk is a chance to find puddles, worms, and overflowing gutters.
how_to: Before you go, talk about the weather and what to wear: 'It's raining, so we need boots and a raincoat.' Walk slowly and look for puddles to stomp in, worms, bugs, and running water.
safety_notes: Avoid deep or moving water and storm drains, and go home if your toddler gets cold.

title: Dance with scarves
summary: Silky scarves and good music invite your toddler to dance, wave, and move to rhythm.
how_to: Play a song with a clear beat, from a real recording or instrument. Give your toddler a light scarf and wave yours fast and slow to match the music. Try a rain stick or maracas for a different sound.
safety_notes: Put scarves away after play and never tie them around the neck.

title: Light and colour at the window
summary: A prism or small mirror in a sunny window scatters light and rainbows for your toddler to chase.
how_to: Hang a prism or a small shatterproof mirror in a sunny window. When light spots and rainbows appear on the floor or wall, point them out and let your toddler chase and touch them. Notice how they move through the day.
safety_notes: Hang the prism out of reach and use shatterproof materials.

title: Kick a ball outside
summary: A big, light ball in an open outdoor space invites your steady walker to try kicking.
how_to: Take a large, light ball to a park or yard. Show how you walk up and kick it gently, then let your toddler try. Walking into the ball counts. Chase it together and kick it back.
safety_notes: Play on grass away from roads and hard edges.

title: Walk the chalk line
summary: You draw a chalk line and give simple directions like 'walk along it' or 'stand at the end.'
how_to: Draw a long line on the pavement with chalk. Ask your toddler to walk along it, then to stand at the beginning, middle, or end. Draw a few more lines and count them out loud together.
safety_notes: Use a quiet driveway, patio, or path away from traffic.

title: Standing throw toward a basket
summary: After sitting throws at 15 months, your toddler now throws a soft ball forward while standing with support.
how_to: Have your toddler stand holding a low table with one hand, or hold their hips. Put a basket a short distance in front of them and let them throw a soft ball or crumpled paper toward it. Move the basket farther away as their aim improves.
safety_notes: Throw soft things only, and explain that we throw at the basket, not at people.

title: Bead threading on a pipe cleaner
summary: Large beads on a pipe cleaner are a step up from rings on a stick: steady enough to thread but bendy, so your toddler holds it with one hand and threads with the other.
how_to: Put 5-6 large wooden beads in a small bowl with a pipe cleaner. Fold over one end so beads can't slide off. Hold the pipe cleaner for your toddler at first, then let them hold it and thread themselves.
safety_notes: Small parts are a choking hazard. Stay within reach and put pieces away after play. Fold over the sharp pipe cleaner ends.

title: Sticker tray
summary: Your toddler peels stickers off a sheet and presses them onto a card, holding the sheet with one hand.
how_to: Put a sheet of large, easy-peel stickers and a few index cards on a tray. Show how you lift a sticker's edge and press it on the card. Once large stickers are easy, offer smaller ones.
safety_notes: Watch that stickers stay out of mouths and noses.

title: Scoop yogurt with a spoon
summary: After trying a fork at 16 months, your toddler moves from a preloaded spoon to scooping thick foods on their own.
how_to: Serve something thick like yogurt or oatmeal. Preload the spoon and rest it on the bowl edge with the handle toward your toddler. Once they can bring it to their mouth, let them try scooping. Model slow scoops with your own spoon.
safety_notes: Offer soft, toddler-safe pieces and keep your child seated while eating to lower choking risk. Expect mess.

title: Dot sticker body parts
summary: You put dot stickers on body parts and play 'Where is your nose? Your elbow?'
how_to: Stick dots on your toddler's knee, hand, and tummy and on your own. Ask, 'Where is your nose?' and let them find the dot or touch the part. Hide a dot somewhere on yourself and let them find it.
safety_notes: Keep stickers away from eyes and supervise so they aren't swallowed.

title: 'Where's the fish?' book pointing
summary: You point to pictures and name them, then ask your toddler to point when you name something.
how_to: With a favourite book, point and name: 'This is a fish.' On later pages ask, 'Where's the dog?' and wait. If they don't point, point for them and name it again. Keep it light; it isn't a test.

title: Action words with gestures
summary: You pair common verbs like eat, drink, open, and wash with a gesture, and use them in different situations.
how_to: Pick a few action words: eat, drink, open, close, wash. Use a gesture each time, like lifting a pretend cup for 'drink.' Repeat the same word in different places: 'wash' your hands, the doll, the carrots. Try leaving a word out of a familiar song for your toddler to fill in.

title: Doll bath with comfort
summary: Through pretend play, your toddler practises comforting a doll who 'gets water in its eyes.'
how_to: Give your toddler a doll, a washcloth, and an empty bowl, and take turns pretend-washing it. Pretend water gets in its eyes and say, 'Oh no, baby is sad, what should we do?' Wipe its eyes and give it a hug, then let your toddler comfort it. Afterward tell them, 'You helped baby feel better.'

title: Choose a shirt, push an arm through
summary: You offer two clothing choices and let your toddler help push arms and legs through.
how_to: Hold up two shirts and go with the one your toddler looks at or grabs. As you dress them, pause at each step: 'Push your arm through,' 'Lift your foot.' Wait for them to do it.

title: Play beside one friend
summary: Toddlers this age usually play next to another child rather than with them; a small playdate with similar toys supports this.
how_to: Invite one friend over and set out duplicate toys, like two sets of blocks. Let the children play side by side at their own pace. Model joining in: 'Sara is lining up blocks. I'll try that too.' It's fine if your toddler just watches.

title: Sort laundry by owner
summary: Your toddler helps with laundry by finding whose clothes are whose and pulling them out of the dryer.
how_to: Let your toddler open the dryer door and pull clothes into a basket. Then sit with a small pile and ask, 'Can you find your shirts? Can you find Daddy's socks?' Make two piles together.
safety_notes: Keep detergent pods and liquids out of reach, and close the machine doors after play.

title: Lock and key tray
summary: A simple padlock with its key tied to a tray gives your toddler a posting-style challenge.
how_to: Tie a padlock's key to a tray with yarn so it can't get lost. Put the open lock on the tray. Show slowly how the key goes in. At first they'll just insert and remove the key; turning it comes later.
safety_notes: Keep the yarn short so it can't wrap around a neck, and supervise; keys are small.

title: Block soup
summary: Symbolic play starts here: blocks in a bowl become pretend soup to stir and 'eat.'
how_to: Give your toddler a bowl, a spoon, and a few small blocks. Put blocks in the bowl and stir: 'I'm making soup!' Pretend to taste it and offer some to them or a doll. Follow their lead if they change the game.
safety_notes: Use blocks too large to swallow.

title: Marks on different surfaces
summary: Your toddler tries different mark-making tools on surfaces like paper, cardboard, and smooth stones.
how_to: Set out two or three tools (chunky crayon, thick brush with paint, chalk) and two or three surfaces (big paper, cardboard, a flat stone). Let your toddler try each tool on each surface. Listen together to the different sounds and describe the marks rather than asking what they drew.
safety_notes: Use non-toxic materials and supervise; chalk and crayons will be mouthed.

title: Potty in the bathroom
summary: With a potty available and calm talk about using it, your toddler can sit on it and copy family members before they are ready to use it.
how_to: Put a potty in the bathroom and let your toddler sit on it, clothed or not, when others use the toilet. Talk about body functions in a matter-of-fact way during diaper changes. Dress them in elastic-waist pants they can start pushing down.
safety_notes: Keep the toilet lid closed and the bathroom door shut when not supervised, and redirect water play to the sink.

title: Potting station
summary: A small tub of soil, a scoop, seeds, and a watering can let your toddler help grow something.
how_to: Set up a low tub of potting soil, a scoop, a few pots, and large seeds like beans. Show how to scoop soil into a pot, press a seed in, and water it. Water the pots together each day and watch for sprouts.
safety_notes: Seeds and soil are not for eating; supervise closely, wash hands after, and choose seeds that aren't toxic.

title: Rescue the critters
summary: Your toddler fetches soft animals from across the room and brings each one home to its pocket.
how_to: Spread soft critters on a couch or coffee table and stand across the room with the pocket holder. Ask, "Can you get the butterfly and bring it home?" Repeat until every critter is back. The stopping, squatting, and reaching build balance and agility.
materials: Quilted Critter Pockets (Lovevery Realist kit) or small soft toys and a basket
safety_notes: Clear the walking path of trip hazards and sharp table corners.

title: Push-and-steer bus
summary: Your toddler pushes a sturdy bus with side handles, steering by shifting their weight.
how_to: Show your toddler how to hold the handles on both sides and push the bus across the floor. Because the wheels pivot, they lean left or right to turn. Add the peg people for a ride when they want to stop and play.
materials: Wheel Around Town Bus (Lovevery Realist kit) or a sturdy push toy
safety_notes: Small peg people are a choking risk for children who still mouth toys; supervise.

title: Cushion mountain
summary: Your toddler climbs up and down a pile of couch cushions to practice balance on an uneven surface.
how_to: Stack couch cushions or pillows on the floor into a low mound. Let your toddler climb up, stand, and come back down. The shifting surface makes them adjust their balance with every step.
safety_notes: Build it on a soft floor away from furniture edges; keep it low and stay within reach.

title: Pouring from a small pitcher
summary: Your toddler pours water from a small pitcher into a glass, a classic Montessori skill.
how_to: Put a small pitcher with a little water and a glass on a tray. Show slowly how to hold the glass steady with one hand and tip the pitcher with the other. Let them pour, then wipe drips together with a cloth.
materials: small pitcher (e.g. Grooved Pitcher & Glass from the Lovevery Realist kit)
safety_notes: Use only a little water and supervise; mop spills right away to avoid slips.

title: Spoon transfer
summary: Your toddler spoons dry beans or rice from one bowl into another.
how_to: Fill one bowl halfway with rice, lentils, or large beans and set an empty bowl beside it on a tray. Demonstrate slowly: hold the full bowl with one hand, scoop, move the spoon over, and tip. Let them work at their own pace; picking up spilled grains is part of the job.
materials: large spoon (a Chinese soup spoon works well)
rice, lentils, or large dry beans
safety_notes: Dry beans and rice are choking hazards; stay close and use larger items if your child mouths things.

title: Pom pom posting carton
summary: Your toddler pokes pom poms through the spout of an empty carton and pulls them out the bottom.
how_to: Cut a flap in the bottom of a clean milk or juice carton. Show your toddler how to push a pom pom through the top spout with a finger, then open the flap to get them back. Repeat as long as they like.
materials: empty milk or juice carton with spout
safety_notes: Pom poms are a choking hazard; keep your toddler within reach and put them away after play.

title: Where is it? game
summary: A simple hide-and-find game that teaches the word "where" by pairing the question with the answer.
how_to: Hide a favorite ball while your toddler watches and ask, stressing the word, "Where did it go?" Find it together and say "Here it is!" Once they get it, ask "Where is the cup?" and see if they find or point to it without help. Focus on one question word for a week or two.

title: Name the kitchen tools
summary: Your toddler plays with real kitchen tools in a bin of lentils while you name each tool and action.
how_to: Put a colander, whisk, measuring spoons, and a muffin tin in a container with a bowl of dried lentils. As your toddler handles each tool, name it and what they do: "You're stirring the lentils with the whisk." Describe size, weight, and texture too.
safety_notes: Lentils are small; supervise closely so they don't go in mouths, noses, or ears.

title: Little helper moments
summary: Give your toddler small chances to help others and point out how it made them feel.
how_to: At bath time, ask your toddler to hand you things just out of your reach. At the playground, if another child drops a toy, help your toddler give it back and name the result: "We handed her the truck and now she has a big smile!"
safety_notes: Stay within arm's reach during bath time; never leave a toddler alone in water.

title: Name it to tame it
summary: When your toddler is upset, describe what happened and name the feeling to help them calm down.
how_to: Calmly put words to the moment: "You really want that toy, and we're not buying it today. That upsets you." If they are mid-tantrum, say little, offer a hug, and breathe slowly. Later, point out feelings in other children and in book characters.

title: Lockbox tinkering
summary: Your toddler works latches and doors on a small lockbox to find what is inside.
how_to: Hide a small favorite object behind one door of the lockbox. Show your toddler one latch slowly, then step back and let them try the others. Hold back on helping unless they ask; trial and error is the point.
materials: The Lockbox (Lovevery Realist kit) or a toy with simple latches
safety_notes: Choose a hidden object too large to swallow.

title: Flashlight on, flashlight off
summary: Your toddler presses a flashlight button to make light and explores what it can light up.
how_to: Dim the room and hand your toddler a child-safe flashlight. Show how the button turns it on and off, then shine it on a wall, a teddy, or under a table. Name what you see in the beam and let them lead where it goes.
materials: toddler-safe flashlight (e.g. Really Real Flashlight from the Lovevery Realist kit)
safety_notes: Use a flashlight with a secured battery compartment; don't shine it in eyes.

title: Animal figure to picture match
summary: Your toddler matches a small animal figure to its photo, linking a real object to a flat picture.
how_to: Lay out 2 or 3 animal pictures and give your toddler the matching figures. Show how to place the cow on the cow picture and make its sound. Add more pairs once they match these easily.
safety_notes: Pick figurines too big to fit in the mouth.

title: Montessori coat flip
summary: Your toddler puts on their own coat with the "tag to the toes, hands in the holes, flip" trick.
how_to: Lay the coat open on the floor, lining facing up. Say "Tag to the toes" and have them stand at the collar, then "hands in the holes" as they slide arms into the sleeves, then "FLIP!" as they swing it over their head. Guide hands at first; if they lose interest, try again in a few weeks.

title: Potty words and easy pants
summary: Prepare for toilet learning by using plain potty words and letting your toddler practice pulling pants down.
how_to: During diaper changes and your own bathroom trips, use matter-of-fact words like "pee" and "poop." Dress your toddler in elastic-waist pants and let them try pushing them down with your help. Move socks or shirts to a low drawer so they can choose clothes.

title: Sound jars and found instruments
summary: Your toddler shakes, taps, and rubs homemade sound jars and everyday objects to hear how they differ.
how_to: Fill a few sealed bottles with different fillings, such as rice, beads, or sand. Put them out with a few safe household objects your toddler can tap or rub together. Watch which sounds they repeat and copy them back.
materials: rice, sand, or beads for filling
safety_notes: Glue or tape lids shut; the fillings are choking hazards if a bottle opens.

title: Hallway obstacle course
summary: A 2–3 station course with a tape balance beam, things to step over, and a ball to kick at the end.
how_to: Make an 8-inch-wide floor "beam" with two strips of painter's tape, add rolled towels to step over, and lay a yardstick across two chairs to duck under. End with a soft ball to kick. Keep it to two or three stations and swap them out on other days.
safety_notes: Check that chairs are stable and the yardstick rests loosely so it falls if bumped.

title: Stair practice between two adults
summary: Your toddler climbs up and down a few stairs between two grown-ups sitting on the steps.
how_to: Sit on one step and have another adult sit a few steps below to fence off a short section. Invite your toddler to go back and forth between you. Let them try going up on their own; going down usually comes later.
safety_notes: Keep the section short with an adult above and below; use a gate when practice ends.

title: Push and pull the laundry basket
summary: Heavy work: your toddler pushes and pulls a weighted basket around the room.
how_to: Put a few books or blankets in a laundry basket and invite your toddler to push it across the floor. Tie a receiving blanket to one handle so they can pull it too. Let them choose what to load and where to haul it.
safety_notes: Use a blanket, not a cord or rope, for pulling, and keep the load light enough to move.

title: Pipe cleaners and a colander
summary: Your toddler threads pipe cleaners into the holes of a colander.
how_to: Start a few pipe cleaners in the colander holes and invite your toddler to pull them out or poke in their own. Show slowly how to line up the tip with a hole. This builds a precise pinch and focus.
safety_notes: Fold over or tape pipe cleaner ends so the wire tips don't poke.

title: Washi tape peeling tray
summary: Your toddler peels strips of washi tape off a tray, building finger strength and concentration.
how_to: Stick several short strips of washi tape on a tray, leaving a corner lifted on each. Show how to pinch the corner and pull. As they get better, press the ends flat so they have to lift them first.
safety_notes: Keep tape scraps away from mouths.

title: Banana peeling
summary: Your toddler peels thick banana slices, holding the fruit with one hand while pulling the peel with the other.
how_to: Cut a banana into thick slices with the peel still on. Show how to hold a slice in one hand and pinch the peel off with the other. Let them eat or serve the slices.
safety_notes: Seat your toddler while eating; cut pieces small enough to chew safely.

title: Talk your way through a book
summary: Use story time to get your toddler talking by expanding on what they say and linking the book to their day.
how_to: When your toddler calls out a word, build on it: "Yes, apples are delicious. Do you think Bea likes apples?" Connect pictures to real life ("You went down a slide this morning!") and pause a few seconds for a reply. Thank them for pointing or turning pages, and stop when interest fades.

title: My First Words photo book
summary: Make a homemade book of photos for the words your toddler already says, then read it together.
how_to: List the words and sounds your toddler says ("doggy," "all done," "moo"). Take or draw a picture for each, label it, and bind the pages with staples or a ring binder. When you read it, let them name each picture and point to the real thing at home.
safety_notes: Adult handles the stapler, glue and any laminating; keep loose photos away from mouthing.

title: Point and name body parts
summary: Name body parts as you point to them on yourself and your toddler.
how_to: During dressing or bath, point and say, "Here's your nose. Here's my nose." Pair each word with the gesture so they can connect the two. Sing a simple, repetitive action song such as "Open, Shut Them" to practice.

title: Comfort the baby doll
summary: Pretend play where you and your toddler wash a doll that gets upset, then comfort it together.
how_to: Pick a familiar, mildly upsetting moment, like water in the eyes at bath time. "Wash" the doll with a washcloth and an empty bowl, then pretend it cries: "Oh no, the baby is sad. What should we do?" Show how to wipe its eyes and hug it, then say, "We helped him feel better."

title: Side-by-side play with doubles
summary: Set up a playmate visit with two of the same toys so toddlers can play next to each other.
how_to: Invite one other child and put out duplicates, such as two sets of blocks, two trucks, or two crayon sets. Model playing beside the friend: "Sara is lining up blocks. I'll try that too. Want to join?" Keep background noise low and let your toddler watch if they prefer.
safety_notes: Check duplicates for small parts if either child still mouths toys.

title: Which one rolls? Ramp test
summary: Your toddler tests a ball, a block, and a peg on a ramp to see which roll and which slide.
