summary: String loop cereal in alternating colors to make a wearable pattern.
how_to: Tape one end of a piece of yarn to the table and wrap the other end with tape to make a stiff tip. Show your child how to thread one color, then another. Say the pattern out loud as they go and tie it off as a necklace.
safety_notes: Supervise closely: cereal can be a choking hazard. Do not let your child sleep or play unattended with the necklace; cut it off after play.

title: Snipping string
summary: Pull a strand of string out of a jar and snip it with child scissors.
how_to: Punch a small hole in a jar lid and thread embroidery floss through it. Show your child how to pull up a little string with one hand and snip with the other. Put the snippets in a small bucket.
materials: small jar with hole in lid
safety_notes: Supervise scissor use; teach that scissors stay at the table. Keep cut string pieces away from younger siblings.

title: Two-year-old Telephone
summary: Pass a whispered word around and practice listening and repeating.
how_to: Choose a word and say it loudly, softly, and in a whisper. Whisper it into your child's ear and ask them to say it in an indoor voice. Switch roles, then send a word around a circle of family members.

title: Favorites, and why
summary: Take turns naming favorite things and explaining why.
how_to: Ask your child their favorite color, food, or animal. Share your own answer with a reason: 'My favorite animal is a dog because they're cuddly.' Ask 'why?' after their answer and keep the back-and-forth going.

title: Read 'The Play Date' and practice joining in
summary: Use a playdate story to rehearse phrases for joining another child's play.
how_to: Read a book about two friends playing and talk about how the characters feel. Practice short phrases together, like 'My turn?' or 'Can I do it?'. Before a real playdate, remind your child of the phrase you practiced.

title: Visual timer for transitions
summary: Use a visual timer so your child can see when an activity will end.
how_to: Before a transition, set a sand timer or visual timer and say, 'When the timer is done, we'll put on our shoes.' Let your child watch the time run out. Use the same timer and phrase every day.

title: Is it the same amount of water?
summary: Pour water between tall and wide glasses and talk about whether the amount changed.
how_to: Fill a tall narrow glass with water while your child watches. Pour it into a short wide glass and say, 'It looks smaller, but it's the same water.' Pour it back. Let your child try pouring both ways.
safety_notes: Use unbreakable cups and supervise all water play.

title: Which two are the same?
summary: Pick out two matching picture cards from a set of three.
how_to: Lay out two identical picture cards and one that is clearly different. Ask your child to find the two that are the same. Ask, 'How did you know?' even if they can't answer yet. Move on to two matched pairs mixed together.
materials: picture cards with pairs (memory game or photos)

title: Color scavenger hunt
summary: Find things around the house that match colored paper squares.
how_to: Spread colored paper squares on the floor and ask your child to name each color. Send them to find an item that matches one square and place it on top. Keep going until each square has a few objects.
safety_notes: Check that collected items are not small enough to swallow.

title: Living room picnic
summary: Host an indoor picnic where your child carries, pours, and serves.
how_to: Spread a spill-friendly blanket on the floor. Have your child carry spoons, napkins, and a small pitcher of water to set up. Serve simple snacks and let your child pour water and serve guests, including stuffed animals.
safety_notes: Cut food into safe sizes and keep your child seated while eating. Expect spills; keep a towel nearby.

title: Flower arranging
summary: Fill a small vase and arrange cut flowers to place around the home.
how_to: Set out a tray with a small pitcher of water, a funnel, small vases, and cut flowers. Show how to pour water through the funnel and place one stem at a time. Let your child choose where the vase goes.
safety_notes: Use non-toxic flowers. Glass vases need supervision; choose sturdy small jars.

title: Rainbows from a window prism
summary: Hang a prism or old CD in a sunny window and explore the light it throws.
how_to: Hang a crystal prism or CD where the sun hits it. Watch together for bands of color on walls and floors. Ask open questions like 'Where did the rainbow go?' and let your child chase it with their hands.
safety_notes: Hang the prism out of reach; glass prisms can break and string is a strangulation risk.

title: Chalkstacle course
summary: Draw a chalk course with a line to run, a spiral to spin, and lily pads for frog jumps.
how_to: Draw a long straight line, a spiral, a zig-zag, and a row of circles on the sidewalk. Assign a movement to each: run, spin, balance, frog-jump. Do the course first, then with your child, then call out the moves while they go alone.
safety_notes: Choose a paved area away from traffic and driveways.

title: Balloon jump
summary: Jump up with both feet to tap a hanging balloon.
how_to: Hang a balloon on a string so it sits just above your child's reach. Show how to bend knees and jump with both feet to tap it. Raise it a little once they reach it easily.
safety_notes: Supervise at all times: popped balloon pieces are a serious choking hazard. Keep the string short and out of reach after play.

title: Pop-up paper tunnel croquet
summary: Roll a ball or push a toy car through paper-arch 'wickets' taped to the floor.
how_to: Fold the ends of a few sheets of cardstock into tabs, bend them into arches, and tape them to the floor. Let your child help place the tape. Roll small balls or push cars through the tunnels, moving slowly so the arches stay up.
safety_notes: Use balls too big to fit in your child's mouth.

title: Match & Tap Hammer Box
summary: Hammer colored pegs into matching holes.
how_to: Show your child how to hold the mallet near the end and tap a peg down. Name the peg color and ask them to find the matching hole. Flip the box and repeat.
materials: Lovevery Match & Tap Hammer Box (or any peg hammer toy)
safety_notes: Teach that the mallet is only for the pegs. Supervise around siblings.

title: Lacing cardboard shapes
summary: Thread yarn through holes punched around cardboard shapes.
how_to: Cut cereal-box cardboard into simple shapes and punch holes around the edges. Tape the end of a 2-foot piece of yarn to make a stiff tip. Show how to push it through a hole and pull it out, then let your child sew freely.
safety_notes: Keep yarn under 2 feet long and put it away after play to avoid strangulation risk.

title: Fork practice with soft cubes
summary: Spear soft food cubes with a child-sized fork at snack time.
how_to: Cut soft foods like banana, cooked sweet potato, or cheese into bite-size cubes. Show how to hold the fork in a fist and push straight down to spear a piece. Let your child feed themselves the whole snack, even if it is slow.
safety_notes: Cut food into small pieces and keep your child seated while eating.

title: Rhyme time
summary: Say rhyming words and invite your child to add one.
how_to: Say a short list of rhyming words, like 'cat, mat, rat.' Ask, 'What's another word that sounds like those?' Accept made-up words. Try new sets at meals or in the car.

title: Your child 'reads' to you
summary: Hand your child a familiar book and let them tell you the story from the pictures.
how_to: Pick a picture book your child knows. Ask them to read it to you by describing the pictures. Ask simple questions like 'What is she doing?' or 'Why is he sad?' and answer your own question if they get stuck.

title: New words to an old song
summary: Change the words of a familiar tune to describe what your child is doing.
how_to: Use a tune your child knows, like 'The Wheels on the Bus.' Swap in new words about toys or daily life: 'The people in the car go up and down.' Invite your child to suggest the next line.

title: Name the feeling with a rich word
summary: Label your child's emotions with specific words like 'disappointed' or 'frustrated'.
how_to: When your child is upset or excited, describe what happened and name the feeling: 'You got the yellow cup, not the blue one. You're disappointed.' Use a new emotion word every few days. Name your own feelings too.

title: Gratitude at the table
summary: Start a mealtime ritual where everyone shares one thing they're thankful for.
how_to: At one meal a day, go around the table and each say one thing you're grateful for. Go first so your child hears an example. Accept simple answers like a pet or the food on the plate.

title: Bean sort: color, then size
summary: Sort beans by color, then mix them up and sort by size.
how_to: Give your child black and white beans and two bowls; ask them to sort by color. Mix them back together, add a bigger type of bean, and sort by size instead. Talk about how the rule changed.
materials: dried beans in two colors and one larger type
safety_notes: Dried beans are a choking hazard and can be pushed into noses or ears. Supervise closely and put them away after play.

title: Tea party
summary: Serve pretend tea and snacks to stuffed animal guests.
how_to: Set out cups, a teapot, and plates. Invite your child to choose stuffed-animal guests and pour pretend tea. Use stand-ins like wooden blocks for cookies and chat with the guests.
materials: toy or real unbreakable tea set

title: Moon sand
summary: Mix flour and oil into moldable sand for scooping and building.
how_to: Pour 4 cups of flour into a bin and add 1/2 cup of vegetable oil. Mix with a spoon. Add cups, spoons, or toy trucks and let your child mold and dig. Store in an airtight container for up to a month.
safety_notes: Taste-safe but not food; discourage eating. Check for wheat allergy. Spread a sheet underneath for easy cleanup.

title: Independent handwashing station
summary: Set up the bathroom so your child can wash and dry hands alone.
how_to: Put a sturdy step stool at the sink, a small soap bar or easy pump, and a hand towel within reach. Show the steps slowly: wet, soap, rub, rinse, dry. Let your child do it themselves before meals.
safety_notes: Set the water heater to a safe temperature and teach which tap is cold.

title: Painting with shells and rocks
summary: Offer paint alongside shells or rocks and see what your child discovers.
how_to: Set out paper, a few paint colors, and a basket of shells or smooth rocks. Don't give instructions; let your child paint the objects, print with them, or arrange them. Ask, 'Tell me about what you made.'
safety_notes: Use large shells and rocks that cannot be swallowed. Use non-toxic paint.

title: Tape hopscotch, single squares
summary: Jump through a simple tape hopscotch made of single squares.
how_to: Mark a column of 4–6 squares on the floor with tape and write a number in each. Show your child how to jump with both feet from square to square. Once that is easy, toss a bean bag into a square and jump over it.
materials: bean bag or small stuffed animal
safety_notes: Tape on a non-slip floor and keep the area clear of furniture.

title: Balloon paddleball
summary: Keep a balloon in the air with homemade paper-plate paddles.
how_to: Tape a craft stick to each of two paper plates to make paddles. Blow up a balloon and tap it back and forth. If hitting is hard, toss the balloon straight at your child's paddle so they succeed.
safety_notes: Supervise closely: popped balloon pieces are a serious choking hazard. Throw away broken balloons right away.

title: Balance on logs and low walls
summary: Walk along a log, curb, or low wall outdoors and jump off at the end.
how_to: On a walk, look for a low log, curb, or garden edge. Offer a hand at first, then let your child balance alone. At the end, show how to jump off and land with both feet.
safety_notes: Stay within arm's reach and choose surfaces no higher than knee height. Avoid wet or mossy logs.

title: Bead threading on a cord
summary: Thread large beads onto a stiff cord, a step up from the cereal necklace.
how_to: Give your child a stiff cord or a shoelace with a knot at one end and a small bowl of large beads. Show how to hold the cord tip near the end and push a bead on. Let them unthread and start again as often as they like.
safety_notes: Use beads larger than a choke-test size and supervise. Store cords out of reach after play.

title: Peg forest in dough
summary: Push pegs into a mound of modeling dough and figure out how to make them stand.
how_to: Set out a lump of modeling dough and a handful of wooden pegs. Make a mound and stand a few pegs in it to start. Let your child pinch, twist, and add dough until the pegs stay upright.
safety_notes: Supervise small pegs. Homemade dough is high in salt; discourage eating.

title: Dot-to-dot pom pom gluing
summary: Glue pom poms onto matching colored dots.
how_to: Put colored stickers or marker dots on a large sheet of paper. Give your child pom poms in the same colors, a small bowl of glue, and a brush. They brush glue on a dot and press the matching pom pom on top.
safety_notes: Pom poms are a choking hazard; use large ones and supervise. Use non-toxic glue.

title: What am I? Sound guessing
summary: Make an animal or vehicle sound and have your child guess what it is.
how_to: Say, 'What animal am I? Moo!' and let your child guess. Use easy sounds first, then harder ones. Let your child make sounds for you to guess.

title: Listening walk
summary: Go outside, stand still, and name the sounds you hear.
how_to: Take a short walk and stop to listen. Ask, 'What do you hear?' Name sounds together: birds, cars, wind, a dog. Listen for one specific sound and signal when you hear it.
safety_notes: Hold hands near roads.

title: Practice 'Space, please'
summary: Rehearse words to use when another child does something your child doesn't like.
how_to: Role-play with a stuffed animal that grabs a toy or stands too close. Help your child say, 'I don't like that' or 'Space, please.' During real play, point out other children's faces: 'She's frowning. I think she wants her spot back.'

title: Talk about feelings in stories
summary: Pause during reading to talk about how characters feel and what might help.
how_to: While reading, stop on a page where a character is hurt, scared, or excited. Ask, 'How do you think he feels? What could we do to help?' Connect it to your child's own experiences and make the faces together.

title: Grace and courtesy by example
summary: Model please, thank you, and pushing in your chair so your child absorbs them.
how_to: Say please and thank you to family members in your child's hearing. Push in your chair after meals and invite your child to do the same. When your child is helpful, thank them for the specific action.

title: First, next, last
summary: Describe daily routines in order to build an early sense of time.
how_to: During bedtime or getting dressed, narrate the steps in order: 'First bath, next teeth, last a story.' Ask your child what comes next. Use a timer to show how long a step will take.

title: Balance scale exploring
summary: Fill the buckets of a balance scale with small objects and see which side goes down.
how_to: Put a simple balance scale on a tray with a basket of small objects. Let your child add items and watch the scale tip. Ask, 'Which side is heavier? How can we make them even?'
materials: assorted small objects (blocks, pinecones, toy cars)
safety_notes: Choose objects too big to swallow.

title: Setting the table with a utensil tray
summary: Carry a tray of utensils and set a place for each family member.
how_to: Store placemats, cups, and utensils down low. Start with one job, like putting out forks. Use a tray so your child can carry several items in one trip. Add plates and cups over time.
safety_notes: Leave sharp knives off the tray.

title: Mud kitchen
summary: Mix soil, sand, water, and nature finds into pretend meals outdoors.
how_to: Set up a corner of the yard with old pots, pans, spoons, a big jug of water, and access to dirt or sand. Add flowers, pebbles, and sticks. Let your child mix 'soups' and 'cakes' and serve them to you.
safety_notes: Supervise water. Remind your child that mud food is not for eating. Wash hands afterward.

title: Walk the line carrying a tray
summary: Walk along a taped line while carrying a small tray with one object on it.
how_to: Make a large oval with tape on the floor. Walk it slowly, heel to toe, carrying a small tray with a block or empty cup. Invite your child to follow. Add a bell or a cup with a little water as they get steadier.
safety_notes: Use unbreakable items and keep the path clear.

title: Action dice obstacle course
summary: Roll a homemade dice and do the action shown: jump like a frog, spin, stomp.
how_to: Tape pictures or words for six actions onto the sides of a cube-shaped box. Your child rolls it and does the action: frog jump, spin in a circle, stomp like an elephant. Add a hoop or tape line to jump into between rolls.
safety_notes: Keep the play area clear of hard furniture edges.

title: The floor is lava
summary: Jump between cushions and pillows without touching the floor.
how_to: Spread sofa cushions and pillows across the floor a short step apart. Tell your child the floor is lava and they must stay on the cushions. Spread them farther apart as jumping improves.
safety_notes: Use cushions on carpet or a rug so they don't slide.

title: Build big with boxes
summary: Lift, carry, and stack big cardboard boxes into towers and houses.
how_to: Save five or more shipping boxes and tape them closed. Let your child carry, stack, and knock them down. Turn them into a house for stuffed animals.
safety_notes: Remove staples and plastic packaging. Don't let your child climb on stacked boxes.

title: Wooden Camper with Locking Doors
summary: Unlock, load, and lock the doors of a wooden camper during pretend play.
how_to: Show your child how the locks open and close. Let them load peg people or small toys inside and lock the doors. Pretend to go on a camping trip together.
materials: Lovevery Wooden Camper with Locking Doors
safety_notes: Peg people can be a choking hazard for younger siblings.

title: Straw necklace with a darning needle
summary: Thread short pieces of paper straw onto wool using a blunt needle.
how_to: Cut paper straws into 2 cm pieces. Thread wool through a thick, blunt darning needle and knot the ends. Your child pushes the needle through each straw piece. When it's full, tie it off and cut the needle free.
safety_notes: Use only a blunt needle and supervise. Store needles in a closed case. Cut the necklace off after wear; don't leave it on during sleep.

title: The coat flip
summary: Put on a coat by flipping it over the head.
how_to: Lay the coat on the floor, open side up, with the hood at your child's feet. Your child puts their hands into the sleeves and flips the coat over their head. Practice each time you go out.

title: I Spy
summary: Take turns spotting and describing things you can see.
how_to: Start direct: 'I spy something red' or 'I spy a car seat.' Let your child find it. When they catch on, let them choose something for you to find.

title: Tell a story starring your child
summary: Retell something from your day as a story with your child as the main character.
how_to: Pick a real event, like a trip to the park, and change one detail: everyone is a mouse. Use your child's name for the hero. Pause and ask, 'What happened next?' so they help tell it.

title: Vocabulary basket with a three-period lesson
summary: Teach names for a small set of objects by naming them, then playing finding games.
how_to: Put 3–5 related objects in a basket, like toy farm animals. Name each one clearly. Then play: 'Can you find the goat?' or match objects to pictures. Skip quizzing 'What is this?' with children under 3.
safety_notes: Use objects too big to swallow.

title: Introduce yourself role-play
summary: Act out saying hello, giving your name, and asking someone to play.
how_to: Use puppets or stuffed animals to show a short script: 'Hi, I'm Sam. Do you want to play?' Let your child take a turn, using their own first name. Swap roles so they hear different answers.

title: Check in on a hurt friend
summary: When someone gets hurt, help your child notice and offer help.
how_to: When a child or family member is hurt, describe what you see: 'He's crying and rubbing his knee.' Model checking in: 'Can I help? Would you like help up?' Later, point out when your child shows kindness.

title: Shape sort into two bowls
summary: Sort cards or paper shapes into two containers by shape, then by color.
how_to: Use matching cards with shapes, or cut circles and triangles from colored paper. Put out two bowls and sort one shape into each. Later, ignore shape and sort by color instead.
materials: shape cards (e.g., Lovevery Reach For The Stars) or paper shapes

title: Wooden Counting Box
summary: Count blocks as you place them, then pull the number card and watch them tumble.
how_to: Place blocks in the box one by one and count together, touching each block. Pull out the number card and watch them fall. Repeat with a different number.

title: Plan a trip together
summary: Ask your child what you need to bring before going out.
how_to: Before going to the park, ask, 'What should we bring?' Build on their ideas and gather the items together. Add weather questions: 'It's sunny. What should we wear?'

title: Dish washing at a low table
summary: Wash a few unbreakable dishes in two bowls of water, then dry them.
how_to: Set two bowls on a low table, one with a little soapy water and one with rinse water. Add a dish brush, drying rack, and towel. Show how to scrub, rinse, and set each dish on the rack, then empty the water into a bucket.
safety_notes: Use lukewarm water and supervise; mop up spills to prevent slipping.

title: Self-portrait in a mirror
summary: Draw a self-portrait while looking in a mirror and at a photo.
how_to: Set a small mirror and a photo of your child on the table with paper and pencils or crayons, including skin tones. Ask, 'Look closely. What shapes and colors do you see?' Accept circles and scribbles; write down what your child says about the picture.
materials: pencils or crayons in skin tones
safety_notes: Use an acrylic or safety mirror.

title: Loose-parts patterns with shells and stones
summary: Arrange shells, stones, and other natural loose parts into patterns and pictures.
how_to: Collect shells, stones, pinecones, and leaves into a basket or clear jars. Set them out on a tray or mat. Let your child sort, line up, or make patterns with no set goal; comment on what you notice.
safety_notes: Use items too big to swallow and check for sharp edges.

title: Hopscotch with pairs and a bean bag toss
summary: Level up from single-square hopscotch to pairs of squares and a bean bag toss.
how_to: Tape a grid of 6–8 squares in pairs. Your child jumps with feet apart into each pair. Then toss a bean bag into a square and jump over that square on the way through. Try hopping on one foot if they're ready.
safety_notes: Tape on a non-slip floor and clear nearby furniture.

title: Yarn 'laser' course
summary: Climb over and crawl under strands of yarn stretched across a hallway.
how_to: Tie or tape yarn or baking twine between furniture legs at different heights. Your child steps over the low strands and crawls under the high ones without touching. Change the layout each round.
safety_notes: Keep strands low and loose, supervise the whole time, and take the yarn down right after play to prevent strangulation or tripping.

title: Move like nature
summary: Imitate trees, rain, birds, and squirrels with your whole body.
how_to: Outside or by a window, point out what nature is doing. Invite your child to sway like a tree, slide down like rain on glass, chirp like a bird, drum like rain, and scurry like a squirrel.

title: Fruit skewers
summary: Thread soft fruit pieces onto a skewer to make a snack.
how_to: Cut soft fruit into chunks. Give your child a blunt skewer or a cut-down straw. Show how to hold the fruit and push it on. Make a rainbow if they're interested, then eat together.
materials: soft fruit (banana, melon, grapes cut in quarters)
safety_notes: Use blunt skewers and supervise; remove skewers before eating. Quarter grapes and cut fruit small to prevent choking.

title: Buttoning practice
summary: Practice opening and closing large buttons on a cardigan.
how_to: Lay a cardigan with big buttons flat on the table. Break the steps down slowly: pinch the button, push it halfway through, pull it from the other side. Let your child try one button at a time.
materials: cardigan or shirt with large buttons

title: Prick work along a line
summary: Poke holes along a simple drawn shape with a prick pen on a felt pad.
how_to: Draw a simple shape, like a circle, on thick paper and place it on a felt pad. Show how to hold the prick pen like a pencil and poke holes along the line. Keep going until the shape can be pushed out.
materials: prick pen or push pin tool
safety_notes: The prick pen is sharp: sit with your child the whole time and store it out of reach.

title: Copy that sound
summary: Make a sound or tone and have your child repeat it exactly.
how_to: Say you're going to make a sound and your child should copy it. Start with simple animal sounds, then make them longer or add a tune. Let your child make sounds for you to copy.

title: Mailbox delivery
summary: Set up mailboxes around the house and deliver 'letters' your child writes.
how_to: Put a small box by each family member, pet, or dollhouse. Give your child junk mail or paper 'letters' to scribble on and deliver. Talk about who each letter is for and what it says.

title: Look back at the photos
summary: Photograph your child's play and creations, then talk through the photos together.
how_to: Take a few photos while your child builds, paints, or plays. Later, look at them together and ask, 'What were you doing here? What happened next?' Write down their words next to a printed photo and display it.

title: Role-play drop-off and pickup
summary: Act out a goodbye ritual so separations feel familiar.
how_to: Pick a short goodbye ritual, like a hug, a kiss, and one more for luck. Play it out at home with your child as the child, then as the parent. Talk honestly: 'You might miss me, and that's okay. Your teacher will help you.'

title: Vet clinic
summary: Care for stuffed animals in a pretend vet clinic.
how_to: Set out stuffed animals, bandages, tape, and toy medical tools. Let your child be the vet while you or a friend bring in 'patients.' Ask, 'What's wrong with your dog? How can we help him feel better?'
safety_notes: Use only toy medical tools; keep real medicines and small bandage wrappers out of reach.

title: Grading nuts and bolts
summary: Match nuts to bolts of different sizes and screw them together.
how_to: Put three sizes of large nuts and bolts on a tray. Show how to find a nut that fits and twist it on. Use words like big, bigger, biggest as your child works.
materials: large nuts and bolts in 3 sizes
safety_notes: Use large hardware that can't be swallowed, and count pieces after play.

title: Mystery bag
summary: Feel objects inside a bag without looking and guess what they are.
how_to: Put a few familiar objects in a cloth bag: a spoon, a ball, a block. Your child reaches in without looking and describes what they feel, then guesses. Pull it out to check.
safety_notes: Avoid sharp objects and anything small enough to swallow.

title: Light table with transparent loose parts
summary: Sort and stack translucent shapes and gems on a light table.
how_to: Set up a light table or a clear storage bin with a light inside. Offer translucent pattern blocks, magnetic tiles, or colored chips. Let your child stack, sort by color, and watch colors overlap.
materials: light table or clear bin with LED lights
translucent shapes, magnetic tiles, or gems
safety_notes: Gems and chips are choking hazards; choose large pieces and supervise. Keep cords tucked away.

title: Mix colors in playdough
summary: Knead two playdough colors together and watch a new color appear.
how_to: Give your child one ball of red and one of blue playdough. Have them squish and knead them together. Watch it marble and turn purple. Ask what colors they want to try next.
safety_notes: Homemade playdough is high in salt; discourage eating.

title: Potting station
summary: Scoop soil, plant seeds, and water them.
how_to: Set up a tray with a bag of soil, a scoop, small pots, seeds, and a watering can. Show how to fill a pot, poke a hole, drop in seeds, and cover them. Water a little each day together.
safety_notes: Wash hands after handling soil. Seeds are small; supervise.

title: Squeeze orange juice
summary: Twist orange halves on a hand juicer and pour the juice.
how_to: Cut oranges in half. Show your child how to press and twist a half on a hand juicer. Pour the juice into a small jug and let them pour it into cups for the family.
safety_notes: An adult cuts the oranges. Juice can sting small cuts.

title: Jump from a step onto cushions
summary: Jump with both feet from a low step onto a soft landing spot.
how_to: Stack sofa cushions at the bottom of a low step. Show how to bend knees, jump off with both feet, and land on the cushions. Move the landing spot a little farther as your child gets confident.
safety_notes: Use only the bottom step and stay within arm's reach. Put cushions on carpet so they don't slide.

title: Laundry basket basketball
summary: Throw soft balls into a laundry basket hung on a door handle.
how_to: Hang a light laundry basket on a door handle or set it on a chair. Give your child soft balls or rolled socks. Have them throw from a short line and step back after each basket.
safety_notes: Use soft balls only, away from windows and breakables.

title: Puddle stomping
summary: Put on rain gear and jump in puddles with both feet.
how_to: After rain, dress in waterproof boots and clothes and head out. Find puddles to jump into with both feet. Compare small splashes and big splashes.
safety_notes: Stay away from roads, deep water, and storm drains. Supervise near any standing water.

title: First sewing with a blunt needle
summary: Sew in and out of loose-weave fabric or card with a blunt darning needle.
how_to: Thread a blunt darning needle with yarn and knot the end. Show how to push the needle down, then pull it up from underneath. Use loose-weave fabric in a hoop or card with holes. Keep the needle in a needle case when done.
materials: burlap in a hoop or punched card
safety_notes: Use only a blunt needle, supervise, and store needles in a closed case out of reach.

title: Getting-ready station for shoes
summary: Find shoes in a basket, sit on a stool, and put them on alone.
how_to: Set up a stool and a shoe basket by the door. Teach the routine: find shoes, sit, try to put them on. Show how to cross a foot over the knee and slide the toes in. Put half a sticker in each shoe so they make a whole picture when placed correctly.
safety_notes: Use a low, stable stool on a non-slip floor.

title: Colored pencil tray
summary: Draw freely with short colored pencils kept ready on a tray.
how_to: Put half-sheets of paper and a few short colored pencils on a tray your child can reach. Sit and draw alongside them. If they're interested, draw a circle and invite them to try one.

title: Sausage
summary: Ask silly questions; the only allowed answer is 'sausage!'
how_to: Ask your child a question like 'What did you brush your teeth with?' They must answer 'sausage!' without laughing. Swap roles and let them ask you questions.

title: Wonder out loud together
summary: Ask open questions about what you see and work out answers together.
how_to: When something catches your child's eye, ask, 'How do you think the ducks float?' or 'What do you think they eat?' Listen to their theory before offering yours. Encourage their own why questions.

title: Sandpaper letter for their name
summary: Trace a textured letter while saying its sound, starting with the first letter of your child's name.
how_to: Use a sandpaper letter book or card. Guide your child's finger over the first letter of their name while saying its sound. Say their name and listen for the sound together.

title: Lunchbox practice at home
summary: Pack a lunch and eat it at the kitchen table to practice preschool routines.
how_to: Pack a simple lunch in the box your child will use. Let them open it, unwrap and open containers, and eat at the table. Talk about who will be at school to help them.
safety_notes: Cut food into safe sizes and stay nearby while your child eats.

title: Making dough together and taking turns
summary: Take turns adding ingredients and kneading bread dough with a friend or sibling.
how_to: Pre-measure the ingredients. Children take turns adding them and stirring; name who is next: 'After Polly, it's your turn.' Give each child a piece of dough to knead with the heel of the hand.
safety_notes: An adult handles the oven. Wash hands before and after; raw dough is not for eating.

title: Thankful jar
summary: Decorate a jar and fill it with notes about what your family is grateful for.
how_to: Decorate a large jar together. Keep paper and pencils nearby. Ask your child what they're grateful for, write it down or let them draw, and have them drop it in. Read the notes together at the end of the month.
safety_notes: Supervise glue and glitter.

title: Hot! Using oven mitts
summary: Practice the word 'hot' and using oven mitts while helping in the kitchen.
how_to: Show your child your oven mitts and say, 'The oven is hot. We use mitts.' Let them put on child-sized mitts and carry a cool tray. While you cook, point to hot pans and the stovetop and ask, 'Is that hot or cool?'
safety_notes: Keep your child away from the stove and oven while they're on. Turn pot handles inward.

title: Scaffolded 12-piece puzzle
summary: Build a 12-piece jigsaw a few pieces at a time.
how_to: Give your child only the top four pieces first. When those are done, add the middle four, then the bottom four. Over time, offer all the pieces at once.

title: Solid Wood Stacking Boulders
summary: Find ways to balance many-sided wooden 'boulders' into towers.
how_to: Set out the boulders and let your child experiment with stacking. When a tower falls, ask, 'Which side sat flat? What could you try?' Build one together and take turns adding a piece.

title: Shadow theater box
summary: Shine a flashlight behind a tissue-paper screen and tell stories with shadow figures.
how_to: Tape tissue or tracing paper over the open side of a cardboard box. Darken the room and shine a flashlight from behind. Move animal figures between the light and screen and watch the shadows grow and shrink. Take turns being the light operator and the audience.
safety_notes: Never shine the flashlight in anyone's eyes.

title: Watering and misting plants
summary: Water houseplants with a small can or mister and wipe up drips.
how_to: Give your child a small watering can and a spray mister. Show which plants need a little water and which like misting. Keep a cloth nearby so they can wipe spills.
safety_notes: Check that houseplants are non-toxic to children.

title: Folding laundry and matching socks
summary: Fold small towels and match pairs of socks from the clean laundry.
how_to: Give your child washcloths and show how to fold them in half and in half again. Pour out clean socks and ask them to find pairs. Let them carry the folded pile to the right drawer.
